headline: Medium-risk pair: shared MCP and browser/network surfaces create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways; no direct evidence of isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use MCP, browsers, and broad network egress; MemMachine also exposes an MCP server. That creates a plausible default bridge where content from one agent can reach the other through shared MCP or copied outputs. No isolation or provenance controls are documented for either agent, so the interaction is not blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected through the same MCP server or message bus
IF LightAgent forwards browser-derived content into MemMachine without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable shared MCP routing between the agents
Insert a provenance tag on every cross-agent message
Require human review before MemMachine consumes LightAgent output
Restrict LightAgent browser output to sanitized summaries
requires-engineering: add content-safety filters at the MCP boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and provenance metadata, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. Because both expose MCP/API surfaces and LightAgent has broad egress, a shared workspace or forwarded context could leak sensitive data across the pair in default integrations. No documented data-isolation mechanism is shown.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to exchange conversation state or memory through MCP
IF LightAgent sends tool results or memory into MemMachine's context window
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Block transfer of raw memory blobs between agents
Redact secrets from LightAgent outputs before forwarding
Limit MemMachine ingestion to user-approved fields only
requires-engineering: enforce field-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent supports subprocesses, browsers, network egress, and multiple instances; MemMachine exposes an MCP server and REST/Python SDK. Even without explicit shared-write permissions, overlapping mutable surfaces can conflict if both are pointed at the same backend or state store. The profiles do not show locking, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared state store or MCP-backed resource
IF multiple LightAgent instances operate concurrently against MemMachine state
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate state namespace
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Disable concurrent LightAgent instances on shared resources
Audit for overlapping API mutations before deployment
requires-engineering: add distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can emit tool results and workflow state, and MemMachine is designed to consume conversational context through API or MCP. That makes it plausible that MemMachine treats LightAgent output as authoritative input, creating a default cascade from one agent's generated content into the other's downstream behavior. No verification step is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF MemMachine ingests LightAgent outputs without an explicit verification step
IF LightAgent-generated facts are used as prompts or memory updates
mitigations: Require source citations on all forwarded facts
Add a verification gate before MemMachine acts on LightAgent output
Use a separate reviewer agent for high-impact actions
Log and diff every cross-agent handoff
requires-engineering: implement structured validation schemas

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent requests API keys and handles broad user/workflow data, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. The profiles do not show residency, retention, or certification mismatches, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: sensitive data may be retained across both systems without a documented deletion/export workflow. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data handling.
conditions: IF the deployment stores regulated user facts in MemMachine and secrets in LightAgent
IF deletion or export requests must propagate across both systems
mitigations: Document which data class lives in which agent
Set a shared retention schedule
Test deletion propagation end-to-end
Avoid storing secrets in either agent unless necessary
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
